customer_updates.text:
The Malabar Hill Elevated Nature Trail offers a calm and well-managed experience, especially for those looking for a quiet break from Mumbai’s chaos.
The entry and exit process is smooth, well-organized, and handled professionally. The security staff deserve special mention—they’re polite, helpful, and clearly serious about their responsibility, which adds to a feeling of safety and discipline.
The walkway itself is quite small, and this is where expectations need to be realistic. While many trees and birds are tagged with names, actual wildlife sightings are limited. During my walk, I only spotted Indian parrots and crows—interestingly, two types of crows: one completely black and another with a grey neck, the kind commonly seen across the country.
The environment is quiet and peaceful, and you do feel good walking there. However, it is not very dense or forest-like, which was a disappointment for me. If you’re expecting a rich, immersive nature trail, this may feel underwhelming. The short length of the walkway further adds to that feeling—it ends just when you start settling into the experience.
Overall:
A neatly maintained, calm space with good management and discipline. Best suited for a short, relaxed walk and first-time visitors. Don’t expect dense greenery or a long trail—think of it as a brief nature pause rather than a full escape into the wild.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik B.
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the Malabar Elevated Nature Trail yesterday and it turned out to be a beautifully planned and refreshing experience. It offers a completely different perspective of Mumbai compared to the usual views from Nariman Point or Marine Lines. This side feels quieter, greener, and far more immersive.

I had booked the 6 am to 7 am slot to catch the sunrise, and it was absolutely worth it. Around 6:13 am, the trail slowly transitioned from darkness to soft morning light and then into a warm sunlit path. Watching that gradual change while surrounded by greenery made the experience feel very special. Even in peak summer, the trail remains surprisingly lush.

At that hour, the environment is calm and soothing. You can hear birds chirping, feel the gentle sea breeze, and enjoy a peaceful start to the day before the city gets busy. The weather is generally pleasant early on, though a bit of humidity is possible depending on the day.

One thoughtful aspect of the trail is the informative signage placed along the way. There are well designed metal information panels that describe the trees, plants, birds, insects, and small wildlife you might come across, with details provided in both Marathi and English. It adds an educational layer to the walk and helps you connect more deeply with the surroundings.

A few things to keep in mind. Entry is strictly through pre booked tickets, so it is best to book a few days in advance as there is no on the spot booking. There is no parking available, so public transport is the way to go. Your ticket is required for both entry and exit, so keep it handy and make sure your phone is charged.

Visitor numbers are limited to around 200 people per slot, which helps maintain the peace and cleanliness of the space. The trail is currently very well maintained, and it would be great if everyone continues to respect that.

It feels like a thoughtful initiative inspired by places like Singapore, and credit to BMC for creating something like this in the city. Hopefully, more such spaces come up across Mumbai.

Overall, this is a must visit if you enjoy nature, calm surroundings, and unique views of the city.

Review of Malabar Hill and Girgaon Beach

Our recent visit to Malabar Hill was inspired by a social media reel by a travel blogger showcasing the new bridge. Unfortunately, the information was inaccurate as the bridge was not open for visitors yet. It seems like the bridge has been overhyped, which was disappointing. So, don’t fall for the hype and waste your time if you’re only visiting for this.

That said, Malabar Hill itself never fails to charm with its timeless appeal. The vintage architecture, well-maintained roads, and excellent traffic management by the Mumbai Police make it a pleasant experience to explore the area.

While at Malabar Hill, we made a stop at Girgaon Beach, which turned out to be the highlight of the trip. If you’re visiting, don’t miss the stunning sunset views—especially in the evening when the beach comes alive with a serene and picturesque atmosphere. It’s truly worth a visit and a great way to end the day.

In summary, while the bridge was a letdown, Malabar Hill and Girgaon Beach still offer plenty of reasons to visit. Go for the classic charm, not the hype!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting Lok Bhavan felt like a long-awaited wish come true. For years, I had wondered what it would be like to stand at that far edge of Mumbai, looking across the Queen’s Necklace, and the experience was every bit as special as I had imagined. I would rather not say too much and let the photos do the talking.
What made it even more memorable was how thoughtfully the whole visit was put together. The tour was managed beautifully by a passionate team from the PRO, and the stories they shared brought the sprawling estate to life in such a genuine way. My one heartfelt suggestion would be to reach on time, so you can truly soak in what has to be one of the most refreshing sunrise experiences in the city.
And that morning chai, offered so thoughtfully as part of the experience, somehow tasted even better in that setting. I honestly cannot imagine a better place to enjoy it. This visit has surely earned a place in my family’s core memories, and it feels like one we will look back on with a lot of warmth. If you are lucky enough to get a booking slot online, it is absolutely worth experiencing.

featured_reviews.name: monisha chandrawanshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Raj Bhavan visit was really wonderful. Guided tour was organised by PR dept of Honorable Governor's office. Booking done from their official website. Only 30 visitors allowed daily (except Monday), booking opens on 10th of every month for the next month dates. Tour time 6 am to 8.30 am, and covered entire area developed by British in 1885.

Helipad
Banquet Hall - hosts various dignitaries
Sunrise Point - spotted various dolphins, witnessed sunrise over marine drive skyline.
Devi temple - has ancient idols of Shri Gundi Aai worshipped by Kolis
Raj Bhavan bunker - star spot of the tour. Built in 1885, discovered only in 2016. Beautifully curated museum on India's struggle for Independence.
Darbar Hall - hosts the iconic oath taking ceremonies for Maharashtra govt CM/ministers / chief Justice of Mumbai high court

Tour was wrapped up by the PR officer Mr Umesh himself, who is a great story teller, has deep knowledge of history and keeps his audience wanting for more. Sung National Anthem without recorded song after school (it still gives goosebumps).

ps - we spotted in house peacocks, saw very old trees (>100 yrs old), were served tea & biscuits, parking and washroom facility available.

Shortcut
Forest Park in Powai is an escape from the pollution and the hustle of the city. Here’s why you should take some time off.

What Makes It Awesome
Amidst the sky scrapers at Hiranandani is a green patch that Powai residents look forward to. Forest Park is a non-manicured forest leftover that still retains that old world charm with gazebos and paths lined with rocks. They have a jogging track to run at and seating for you to rest at. Since the rain Gods have been more than gracious off late, we think it would be a treat to sit and admire the weather and smell the rain hitting the mud.

The park sits quietly at Hiranandani Gardens and is frequented by fitness enthusiasts, strollers and college students. It’s open from 6AM in the morning till 10AM and reopens again till 6 PM. The entry to the park is free.

Pro-Tip
If you need some respite from the heat, Forest Park is always a few degrees lesser that the usual temperature outside.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellant place for Morning Walker, kids and families.

HERITAGE GARDEN: De-stressing and Rejuvenating in a Different World

Pramod Chavan

Surrounded by high-rise concrete buildings and glass-fronted skyscrapers opposite the Glen Towers on Cliff Avenue Road in Powai, a Heritage Garden means Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee Udyan is a de-stressing and rejuvenating world.

The special thing about this ten-acre park is that it is not just a park for one class or one age group. On one side are college students on the fence and on the other a group of senior citizens reminiscing. Here, among the youth the guitar tunes, and among the senior citizens, someone easily makes the flute tunes, mesmerizing the entire atmosphere.

Apart from the magnificence of the surrounding residential complexes, it is the right space for yoga enthusiasts with its many offices and commercial setups. It has become a place for those who practice regular and mixed martial arts.

The landscaped lawns, a separate play area for children, a Japanese-style Miyawaki patch on one side and a circular walking path that winds around the periphery of the park make the Heritage Garden a pleasant place to spend an evening with your loved ones.

Heritage Garden is one of the main places for morning walkers in Powai and the surrounding area. There is a beautiful gazebo apart from benches at regular intervals. It also has a beautiful artificial pond which often has beautiful lotus flowers.

The stone structure along the circular walkway attracts the attention of all new visitors. There is also a restroom on one side of the park.

Another special feature of this park is that some other parks in the city often organize events, so people coming to the park have a lot of trouble. However, events or other mass activities are still not allowed here without permission.

The man-made wells located at the corners of the park are used the most during monsoons. But it has not been able to escape from the habit of people coming to the garden to throw large amounts of waste.

Garden gates open at 5 am, after that they are closed from 12 noon to 4.30 pm... and open again from 4.30 pm to 10 pm.

featured_reviews.name: siddesh narvekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Powai Dam is a major reservoir located in Powai, a suburb in the northeastern part of Mumbai, India. It was built in 1891 by the British colonial government to supply drinking water to the city of Mumbai.

The dam is constructed across the Mithi River and covers an area of about 2.1 square kilometers. It has a height of approximately 26 meters and a length of 1,450 meters. The reservoir created by the dam has a capacity of 545 million gallons (2.48 million cubic meters) of water.

The Powai Dam is surrounded by lush greenery and provides a picturesque view. It serves as a popular recreational spot for locals and tourists, offering opportunities for boating and fishing activities. The dam also plays a crucial role in flood control, as it helps regulate the water flow during heavy rains.

Over the years, the Powai Dam has become an important landmark in Mumbai, attracting visitors with its serene atmosphere and scenic beauty. It is considered a significant source of water supply for the city and plays a vital role in meeting the water demands of its residents.

We reached out to Rajith through a friend when we had a day open in our schedule while visiting Cochin, Kerala, and wanted to explore the backwaters. Rajith recommended a silent backwater cruise, and it turned out to be the highlight of our time in Cochin.

The experience was a small, hand punted boat tour through lush, narrow canals, offering a rare glimpse into the quieter, less seen side of the backwaters. The serenity of the surroundings, along with the rich flora and fauna, was truly unforgettable and something that must be experienced in person.

Our guide, Peter, was exceptionally knowledgeable, warm, and deeply connected to the local community. We also enjoyed a delicious home-cooked lunch prepared by a local family and learned how coir rope is traditionally made, which added a wonderful cultural touch to the day.

I would highly recommend Rajith for thoughtfully curated, non-touristy experiences. The backwater tour with Peter and the welcoming villagers was outstanding, and overall, an experience we will remember for a long time.

Our family of four shared eight lovely days in God's Own Country, Kerala, in mid- July. Arranged by The Traveling Gecko, we got an oppurtunity to experience three very different ecosystems in a short period of time. In Kumarakom, where we stayed at the Coconut Lagoon, we were awestruck by the raw beauty of the Backwaters. From there we moved to Vanilla County, a quaint Dutch styled bungalow in Vagamon. It was our first home stay experience and we loved it. This patch of our holiday was a thoroughly relaxed one..The last three days of our vacation was spent at another beatiful property, the Brunton Boatyard, built on an old shipyard. Colonial influence is so evident in the nooks and corners of Fort Kochi and we delighted in the surprises. I think the highlight of our trip was the Village Backwater Tour which totally floored us with the beauty of the backwater canals.

One common thread of this varied holiday was the carefully selected properties. Each of them had a warm and courteous staff with very good food. The same can be said about Shaji, our driver for the entire duration of the stay.
